chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from al-Fadl ibn 'Ayyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: Who is the pious (one of piety/forbearance) among people? He said: The one who is pious from the prohibitions of Allah and avoids these. And if he does not guard against matters of dubiousness, he will fall into the prohibited whilst not recognizing it, and if he sees the evil and does not condemn it whilst having the ability to do so, he has certainly liked for Allah to be disobeyed. The one who likes for Allah to be disobeyed, has certainly challenged Allah with enmity. The one who likes the continuation of the oppressors, has certainly liked for Allah to be disobeyed. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, praised Himself for the destruction of the oppressors, so He said: «So, eliminated were the people who wronged. And praise be to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.»

key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: Piety, forbearance, or scrupulousness in religious matters
key_terms.بَارَزَ اللَّهَ: Challenged Allah directly / faced Allah with enmity

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of war' (piety) and how does avoiding doubtful matters protect one from sin?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive definition of *war'* (piety), emphasizing that true forbearance requires not only avoiding clear prohibitions but also rigorously shunning *shubuhat* (doubtful matters) to prevent inadvertent sin. The text further establishes a theological link between passive acceptance of evil and active enmity toward Allah, culminating in the divine praise for the destruction of the oppressors. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ittiba'* (following) the Imams' practical guidance in distinguishing between the permissible and the doubtful.
